title: You didn’t fall overnight.
paragraphs: It was subtle. Quiet. Almost unnoticeable.

A compromise you justified.
A thought you entertained longer than you should have.
A habit you said you could stop anytime.

Your hunger for God isn’t what it used to be.
Conviction feels distant.
Prayer feels heavier.
Sin feels… easier.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The devil doesn’t need your whole life.
He just needs a foothold.

A crack.
An opening.
A place to stand.
Scripture doesn’t exaggerate this. It warns you directly:
“Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil.” — Ephesians 4:26–27
That means access can be granted.

Not by accident…
but by permission.

You thought it was just anger you didn’t deal with.
Just bitterness you held onto.
Just lust you kept revisiting.
Just pride you refused to surrender.
And every time you allowed it to stay, something spiritual shifted.

Because sin is never isolated.
It opens doors.
Jesus warned about this kind of vulnerability:

“When the unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest… Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ And when it comes, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order. Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself…” — Matthew 12:43–45
An empty life without surrendered obedience doesn’t stay empty.
That’s the part no one tells you when you treat sin casually.

You’re not just “struggling.”
You’re creating access points.

He watches what you tolerate.
What you excuse.
What you hide.
Because what you hide… he builds on.

And suddenly, what once convicted you now comforts you.
What once grieved you now feels normal.
What once felt wrong now feels justified.
“Each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death.” — James 1:14–15
So when you give it space, you’re not managing it.
And the cost isn’t just behavior.

It’s your sensitivity to God.
Your clarity.
Your peace.
Your authority.
Because you can’t walk in spiritual authority while entertaining what crucified Christ.
But here’s the part that changes everything…
“Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” — James 4:7
Most people try to resist without surrendering.
Because the power isn’t in your willpower.
When you fully surrender—your habits, your thoughts, your secret places—something shifts.
And what once had access… has to leave.
But that requires something most avoid:

A decision that says:
“I’m done giving the enemy space in my life.”
And yes… it will cost you.

It will cost your pride.
Your comfort.
Your hidden sins.
Your excuses.
But it will give you something far greater:
And a restored closeness with Jesus that sin could never give you.
So now you’re standing at a line.

One path keeps the door cracked.
The other slams it shut.

One leads to slow spiritual decay.
The other leads to life.
Even if it’s just one word: “Repent.”
Because silence is where sin grows.
But truth is where freedom begins.

There’s more depth waiting for you. More truth that exposes, corrects, and rebuilds what compromise has weakened. Walk deeper into it, not alone, but with guidance rooted in Scripture and sharpened for real transformation.
Follow the journey. Stay where truth doesn’t bend.
